maria (Presales): Hi team — AcmeRetail wants a quick POC next week. They want: 1) token streaming from Python/Node/Rust SDKs 2) function/tool calling for inventory lookups (struct output) 3) SLA/pricing for sustained 10k qps (burst 30k). Any blockers?
eli (Eng): Thanks — main risk is the toolcall schema across SDKs. Node/Python already have structured response helpers; Rust binding is new and needs a tiny adapter.
sam (Solutions): Also need to confirm streaming semantics: do they want SSE or websocket? They mentioned server-side fanout for webhooks.
maria (Presales): They prefer websocket for lower latency. Can we show an example that does a function call + streaming tokens (partial results + final JSON payload)?
eli (Eng): Yep. Example (Node):
```js
const stream = client.chat.stream({model: 'r-infer-1', input: prompt, functions:[{name:'lookup', parameters:{type:'object'}}]});
stream.on('token', t => console.log(t));
stream.on('function_call', fc => console.log('func call', fc));
```
The SDK yields function_call events; final structured output arrives as function_result JSON. Rust will mirror but needs a small enum change.
sam (Solutions): For the POC we can ship a tiny Rust shim that unmarshals the function_result into serde_json::Value. I can draft it.
maria (Presales): Great — what's the ask from Security for the SSO/KMS side? AcmeRetail wants bring-your-own-key + EU residency.
josh (Security): We need: - SOC2 report (we have) - KMS integration options (customer KMS via VPC connector or HSM in Dedicated) - Data residency: can run Dedicated in eu-west-1 or Private in their VPC. Also confirm logs retention and whether user data is stored. I'll attach checklist.
josh (Security): Quick answer: BYOK via our Dedicated + KMS passthrough is supported; Private supports customer-managed HSM. Retention defaults to 30d but can be extended or disabled for Private.
maria (Presales): Perfect. Pricing: can someone ballpark monthly cost for Dedicated at 10k sustained qps? They asked for monthly committed pricing and a 3-month POC discount.
sam (Solutions): Rough calc: 10k qps for chat is heavy. If average response 30 tokens, token/sec = 300k tps ~ huge. More realistic mapping: QPS here means requests/sec — depends on amplification. For planning assume 1 request => 150 tokens generated avg => 1.5M tokens/sec — wait that's off. Let's do per-minute: 10k qps * 150 tokens = 1.5M tokens/sec ~ 90M tokens/min. This is massive; better to clarify expected tokens per request.
maria (Presales): Good catch. I'll ask AcmeRetail for expected avg tokens per request + % streaming vs small completions.
eli (Eng): Operationally we can handle via Dedicated clusters with batching. For POC we recommend throttling to a realistic slice (e.g., 500 qps sustained) to validate integr and telemetry. Then scale.
sam (Solutions): For a 3-month POC: propose Dedicated 4x A100s equivalent reserved, dev discount 50% on list for first 3 months. I'll draft numbers once we have token estimates.
maria (Presales): Action items: 1) I will ask AcmeRetail for avg tokens/request and confirm websocket vs SSE 2) Sam to draft Rust shim and POC runbook 3) Josh to send security checklist + SOC2 pointer 4) Eli to provide a minimal Node+Rust example repo we can share.
eli (Eng): I'll push a sample repo to github and post link here before EOD. Deploy-bot: deploy started for sample runtime (staging).
deploy-bot: Deployment 8731 to staging succeeded :white_check_mark: (logs: https://ci.redwood/internal/8731)
maria (Presales): Thanks — last Q for legal: do we need an NDA before sharing sample code? They are an enterprise but already signed MSA. I'll verify.
sam (Solutions): If MSA in place, code sample is fine. If they want access to dedicated infra, need PO.
maria (Presales): Awesome. I'll update the customer and loop back with tokens estimate.
eli (Eng): One more note on function_call schema: senders should validate both "type":"object" and fallback to raw string if consumers can't parse. That avoids crashes.
maria (Presales): Noted. I'll include that in the POC acceptance criteria. :thumbsup:
